answer: A graph-based trust protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by bounding transitive credit across verified peer interactions. An adversary incurs the scarce cost of building authentic relational history across topological cuts to harbor counterfeit identities, rendering any fabricated fable of prestige ineffective when querying nodes or exchanging violet telemetry data. However, this mechanism introduces steep cold-start latency for honest newcomers and risks cementing incumbent cartels.
